rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TO RESIDENTS OF A REGION WHERE A GEOTHERMAL ENERGY PLANT IS LOCATED A THIRTY PERCENT (30%) DISCOUNT ON THEIR POWER RATE CONSUMPTION
rows.abstract: Rationale:  To compensate the threat posed by these plants, this bill proposes that the residents of the region be given discounted rate for the use of electricity from the geothermal plant located in their region.  This is at least government can do for the people of the region who sacrifice so much in the name of progress. Considering that the entire nation benefits from these plants, it is but fair that the residents who are prejudiced thereby should be granted incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR A COMMUNITY SERVICE PROGRAM FOR CONVICTED PRISONERS, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMUNITY SERVICE CAMPS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Community Service Program Act." Rationale: Exposure to almost normal conditions outside of these prison walls is an opportunity for the convicts to see a better side in life and for the community to benefit from the labor that these convicts can contribute to society. These can also help the convicts as time spent outside the prison walls prevents them from become hardened criminals. It is the hope of the proponent that convicted offenders of less grave offenses need not serve their sentencesin prison but in Community Work Camps where their services can become beneficial to the community and assure the convicts rehabilitation and integration into society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVOLUTION OF THE CONTROL, MANAGEMENT AND OPERATION OF MUNICIPAL OR TERTIARY PORTS FROM THE PHILIPPINE PORTS AUTHORITY TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Municipal Ports Act of 1998."  This bill seeks to devolve the power and authority in the control, management and operation of municipal ports, including the power or revenue collection, from the Philippine Ports Authority to local government units.Such devolution of authority is in consonance with the declared policy of the State, as embodied in the Local Government Code, that local government units shall enjoy genuine and meaningful local autonomy to enable them to attain their fullest development as self-reliant communities and make them effective partners in the attainment of national goals.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING RETIREMENT AGE OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED GSIS ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Rationale: The present retirement age of sixty five and sixty years for government employees could hardly be rewarding to them since they would no longer enjoy the fruits of their retirement. At that age, retirees would either be too old, too weak or too sickly. Reaping the rewards of his government service at a much earlier age enables the retiree to have a better chance of starting a new career.  A younger retiree can prepare himself for a new life such as venturing into his own business or further utilizing his talent for private enterprise. His economic value would be much higher rather than if was sixty-five years of age.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-06

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROGRAM FOR THE ACQUISITION OF SCHOOL SITES AND THE CONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE, REHABILITATION AND REPAIR OF SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN THE PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS NATIONWIDE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHERPURPOSES
rows.abstract: "School Building Program Act of 2001."  The bill seeks to create a comprehensive program which will address the problem of classroom shortage.  A salient feature of this bill is the provision of build-operate-t ransfer, build-lease-tra nsfer, build-transfer, rehabilitate-o perate-transfer , and other contractual arrangements that will allow the use of both government and private funds to finance the construction of needed school buildings, and the creation of an inter-agency committee to formulate and ensure the effective implementation of the program by the Department of Education, Culture and Sports.  The program also provide for the integration of all the necessary information for the effective monitoring and maintenance of existing schhool buildings.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-06

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN AND REFORM THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed bill seeks to achieve greater autonomy in the operations of the Sangguniang Kabataan at all levels. It grants bigger powers and recognition to duly elected youth leaders as partners in nation-building . It is about time that attentionis given to our young not as vulnerable sector requiring protection, but as formidable force to reckon with the present.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-08-06

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AFFORDING PRECTION TO WORKING WOMEN, STRENGTHENING THEIR RIGHTS TO EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN BOTH PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS AND STRENGTHENING THE PROHIBITION ON DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN WITH RESPECT TO THEIR EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to EXPAND the coverage of legal protection against gender discrimination from the time of pre-employment and human resources development to the time of actual employment and labor relations and promotions to the executive level.  Italso provides the mechanisms for the implementation of the same. Furthermore, this bill seeks to expand this statutory protection against discrimination of women workers by providing that all personnel actions in all branches, subdivisions, instrumentaliti es and agencies of the government, including government-owne d and controlled corporations with original charters shall be made free from any discrimination based on sex.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR OPTIMUM PERFORMANCE IN REVENUE COLLECTION THROUGH LATERAL ATTRITION AND GRANTING OF SPECIAL INCENTIVES AND REWARDS FOR EXEMPLARY SERVICE IN REVENUE-GENERAT ING AGENCIES OF GOVERNMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Despite the very important mandate and roles the BIR and BOC have, the two agencies had enjoyed notoriety of sorts for so long. These two, along with the Bureau of Immigration (BID), the Land Transportation Office (LTO) and other revenue-generat ingagencies are often perceived as milking agencies of grafters and corrupt officials and employees.  It is this situation that this bill aims to address. The issue of graft and corruption in revenue-generat ing agencies and/or local government units must be acted upon resolutely, however radically.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PRESIDENTIAL COMMISSION ON GOOD GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: In line with the cost-saving efforts of the new dispensation, this measure proposes to abolish PCGG and its functions transferred to existing government agencies.  The authority to investigate and prosecute ill-gotten wealth cases shall now be vested with the Department of Justice and the authority to dispose recovered assets shall now be transferred to the Asset Privatization Trust (APT).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-06

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING GRADUATES OF PHILIPPINE SCHOOLS OF MEDICINE, NURSING, DENTISTRY AND MED-TECH WHO HAVE NOT TAKEN THEIR BOARD EXAMS IN THE PHILIPPINES BUT WHO HAVE PASSED THE STATE BOARD EXAM IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA TO PRACTICE THEIR PROFESSION IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The Philippines has been experiencing a brain drain in the Medical, Nursing, Med-Tech and Dental professions. In view of this, the country is losing so much in terms of expertise and services that these professionals would have been able to render if they did not chose to leave our country.  This bill is envisioned to provide a way by which this problem maybe countered aside from the fact that our people would be able to take advantage of the expertise that these professionals have earned whilepracticing their respective professions abroad.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CERTAIN INVESTIGATIVE AND PROSECUTORY POWERS TO THE COMMISSION ON AUDIT FOR CRIMINAL OFFENSES PROVIDED FOR UNDER TITLE SEVEN, CHAPTERS THREE AND FOUR OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE OFTHE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Records show that the Commission on Audit have discovered numerous cases of offenses in violation of existing laws, rules and regulations in its exercise of its regular audit functions however, statistics show that investigation and eventual prosecution and perpetrators have been anemic.  It cannot be denied that the Commission on Audit can greatly contribute towards the improvement of this sorry state.  This can only be attained by the Commission on Audit if it can be conferred investigative and prosecutory powers in addition to its existing auditorial powers aside from the fact that this scheme could have decongest the backlog that is now prevailing in the different Prosecutor's Offices of the Department of Justice all over thhe country.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03570

rows.abstract: Principally, the proposed Center shall be tasked to: a. To provide skills training services to develop the individual skills of residents of the municipality for employment and for small scale entrepreneurshi p; b.  To provide the necessary knowledge, technology and training that will cover all aspects of livelihood production such as furniture making, handicrafts, ceramics, garments, pottery, ornamental plants, decor making, wood carving and agri-business production such as poultry, fishery, hog and cattle raising.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE NUMBER OF REGIONAL TRIAL COURT BRANCHES IN THE PROVINCE OF QUEZON AND LUCENA CITY FROM THIRTEEN (13) BRANCHES TO FOURTEEN (14) BRANCHES BY CREATING A NEW BRANCH WITH SEAT AT CATANAUAN, QUEZON, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SUBPARAGRAPH 8 AND PARAGRAPH E OF SECTION 14 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 129

rows.abstract: Rationale: The Magna Carta for Public Schoolteachers had failed to provide benefits to the dependents of teachers. Thus, this bill seeks to grant additional benefits to teachers by giving their dependents the right to scholarship grants, free medical treatment and pension in case of disability of the teachers. In addition, it also encourages teachers to form cooperatives in their own municipalities to help promote their economic welfare.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER AND DATE OF ELECTION OF SECTORAL REPRESENTATIVES TO THE LOCAL SANGGUNIANS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There shall be three (3) sectoral representatives each in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Bayan and Sangguniang Panlungsod who shall be elected pursuant to this Act:  One (1) from the women sector; one (1) from the workers; and one (1) from any of the following sectors: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disable persons and elderly, which may be determined by the sanggunian concerned not later than one (1) year prior to the holding of the next local elections.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05781

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF POLITICAL DYNASTIES
rows.abstract: Any person who has a political dynasty relationship with the incumbent President of the Philippines or a candidate for such elective position is disqualified from running for any national and local elective public office. Any person who has a political dynasty relationship with an incumbent elective official is disqualified from running for any elective public office within the same city and/or province where an incumbent elective public official is also running: Provided, That, the incumbent elected public official covered by this Act shall not include that of Barangay official.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT CLASSIFYING ELECTION OFFENSES, AND PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: INCREASING the penalties for election offenses, as well as the immediate and decisive prosecution thereof, would serve as a deterrent against electoral fraud and violence.  If enacted into law, this vital piece of legislation would contribute to the professionaliza tion and democratization of our political structures towards meaningful economic and social reforms in Philippine society.  In the main, this bill seeks to impose upon the offender the penalties of prision correctional andprision mayor which have the same number of years of imprisonment for serious and less serious election offenses, respectively, under the Election Code of 1978.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-06

rows.author: C060

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING POLITICAL TURNCOATISM AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION SEVENTY-ONE OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. EIGHT HUNDRED EIGHTY-ONE, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Turncoatism, most often, is the result of political patronage, or hope of greater patronage from the party in power.  Party platforms and ideologies are eschewed in exchange for patronage. This practice certainly is preventing and not helping in the development of a strong multi-party system.  In order to minimize politics of patronage and develop a strong multi-party system in the Philippines, it is the purpose of this bill to prohibit political turncoatism and provide penalties thereof.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06418

rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURE FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS HOLDING OF SPECIAL ELECTIONS IN CASE OF VACANCY IN THE CONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY-FIVE, ENTITLED `AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANNER OF FILLING A VACANCY IN THE CONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES'
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 6645, and prescribes the procedure for the expeditious holding of special election, through a certification by the Speaker on the existence of vacancy and calling for a special election to fill the vacancy in a particular legislative district.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-08-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY LABELING OF FOOD AND FOOD PRODUCTS CONTAINING GENETICALLY-MOD IFIED ORGANISMS AND FOOD PRODUCED BY GENETIC ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED AND TWENTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FOOD, DRUGS AND DRUG DEVICES AND COSMETICS ACT, AND REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-FOUR, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONSUMERS' ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Genetically Engineered Food Right to Know Act." Rationale:  In line with the Constitutional mandate for the State to "protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them." and the Constitutional right of the Filipino people "to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature," it is hereby declared the policy of the State to ensure that the Filipino people are provided with safe food and food products that will notput their health at risk and place the environment in jeopardy.

rows.author: C106
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE, ESTABLISHMENT OR CONSTRUCTION OF FUEL DEPOTS AND WAREHOUSES, OR STORAGE OF OTHER FLAMMABLE OR HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS OR SUBSTANCES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This Act shall cover all future and existing publicly and privately-owned fuel depots and warehouses or storage of flammable or hazardous chemicals and substances. These shall include places or establishments not normally intended for such storage or deposits but are actually used for the purpose on a temporary or permanent basis.  The movable character of the depot, warehouse or storage shall not remove the same from the coverage of this Act.  No such depot, warehouse or storage shall be maintained, established, or constructed within a dangerous distance from a populated area or area classified as residential. Conversely, areas within the same radius from such depot, warehouse or storage shall not be classified as residential nor shall acctually be used as such. The distance shall vary depending upon the volume and nature of the stored fuel, substance, or chemical.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2001-08-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE AUTOMATIC DISMISSAL OF DORMANT COURT CASES
rows.abstract: Dormant cases are cases filed with the courts which have not been prosecuted for a period of six (6) months from the date the last pleading was filed or the date the last hearing was held.  The courts shall automatically dismiss dormant cases without need of a motion immediately upon the lapse of the six-month period referred to above.  The order of dismissal shall be mailed by registered mail to all parties.  The order shall become final within fifteen (15) days from receipt thereof.

rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to introduce the Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) which we hope will be accepted as an essential and valuable tool in encouraging savings for our people's retirement years.  A PERA is a savings plan to achieve a comfortable and financially-sec ure retirement through a sound investment and planning scheme. Through a PERA, one is encouraged to save because certain contributions to the savings funds are deductible from the taxable income, and earnings of said savings are sheltered from taxation as they grow and are taxed only upon their withdrawal from PERA.

rows.abstract: "Gifted Children and Science-Oriente d Youth Act." Rationale: Global estimates indicate that 3% of any given population is gifted. Therefore, in population of 12.4M elementary school children and 5.06M high school students, there should be 374,246 gifted elementary school students and 151,985 gifted high school students. Because of the absence of a concerted program to identify and nurture them, these gifted children are deprived of the opportunity of challenging and appropriate instruction which bring out their best.  The national program for these special children focuses on their early identification and nurturance,  A center for the Gifted Children and Science Oriented Youth shall be established at the University of the Philippines tocoordinate the national program.
